config.title: Toggle Visibility (TypeScript)

intro.title: Toggle Visibility — Typed
intro.body: Learn to create interactive UI elements that respond to user clicks while maintaining type safety throughout.
intro.usecase: You'll build a toggle button that shows/hides content, a common pattern in modals, accordions, and settings panels.

objectives: Conditionally render JSX based on state

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use named imports for both React and useState.
steps.whyThisMatters: React provides the building blocks for components, and useState is essential for managing interactive state.

thinkPrompt.question: What do we need from React to create a component with state?
options: Only React itself since state is built-in
React, useState, and useEffect for side effects

steps.anchor: We need both React (for component definition) and useState (for state management).
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are declared at the top of the file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've imported the essential tools for building a stateful component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Remember to import both React and useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. We need React for component creation and useState for state management.

steps.title: Create Component Structure
steps.instruction: Define a function component named ToggleVisibility that returns JSX.Element.
steps.hint: Start with 'function ToggleVisibility(): JSX.Element' or use arrow function syntax.
steps.whyThisMatters: Every React component needs a proper function signature that defines its interface and return type.

thinkPrompt.question: What TypeScript return type should a React component function have?

steps.anchor: A component that renders JSX should use an explicit JSX.Element return type on the function (or on a function declaration).
steps.expectedOutcome: A component function is defined with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: Has an explicit TypeScript return type (JSX.Element)
Has empty JSX return for now
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've established the component's foundation with a clear TypeScript return type.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there. Give the component an explicit TypeScript return type: JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's revisit. Define the component so it explicitly returns JSX.Element (e.g. function ToggleVisibility(): JSX.Element { ... } or const ToggleVisibility = (): JSX.Element => ...).

steps.title: Declare Typed State
steps.instruction: Inside the component, declare a state variable to track visibility, typed as boolean with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use useState<boolean>(false) to create typed state.
steps.whyThisMatters: TypeScript ensures our visibility state is always boolean, preventing runtime errors from incorrect state values.

thinkPrompt.question: What TypeScript type should we use for a visibility toggle state?

steps.anchor: Boolean is the most semantic type for toggle states (visible = true, hidden = false).
steps.expectedOutcome: A boolean state variable and its setter are declared inside the component.
successCriteria: Type is explicitly boolean or inferred
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! You've created type-safe state that will control our visibility.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start. Remember to type the state as boolean and initialize it to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's adjust. We need boolean state initialized to false using useState.

steps.title: Build JSX Structure
steps.instruction: Return JSX containing a button and a content holder element that will display our toggleable content.
steps.hint: Wrap both elements in a parent container like a fragment or div.
steps.whyThisMatters: The JSX defines what users see - a button and conditional content area.

thinkPrompt.question: What JSX elements do we need for a toggle interface?
options: Just a button that changes text
A button and a content element (like a div, p, span, or heading)
thinkPrompt.correctAnswer: A button and a content element (like a div, p, span, or heading)

steps.anchor: We need both the control (button) and a content area (any suitable element) that responds to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: JSX with a button and a content element is returned from the component.
successCriteria: Content element is present to hold the toggleable area
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect structure! You've laid out the visual foundation for our toggle.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost. Make sure you have both a button and a content element that will hold the toggleable content.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. We need a button and a suitable content element for the toggleable area.

steps.title: Create Toggle Handler
steps.instruction: Define a function inside the component that toggles the visibility state between true and false.
steps.hint: Use arrow function syntax and the state setter with previous state.
steps.whyThisMatters: Event handlers encapsulate the logic that responds to user interactions in a type-safe way.

thinkPrompt.question: How should we toggle a boolean state value in React?
options: Use the setter function with current value
Create a handler that calls the setter with !currentValue
thinkPrompt.correctAnswer: Create a handler that calls the setter with !currentValue

steps.anchor: We need a handler function that toggles the boolean state using functional update pattern.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handler function is defined that toggles the boolean state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great handler! It cleanly encapsulates the toggle logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good attempt. Make sure your handler toggles between true and false using the setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's refine. We need a function that toggles the boolean state value.

steps.title: Connect Everything
steps.instruction: Wire the toggle handler to the button's click event and conditionally show the content div only when visibility state is true.
steps.hint: Use onClick for the button and conditional rendering (&&) for the div.
steps.whyThisMatters: Wiring state and handlers to JSX creates the interactive experience users expect.

thinkPrompt.question: How do we make the UI respond to our state and handler?
options: Call the handler directly in JSX
Connect handler to button click and conditionally render content
Just declaring them is enough - React auto-wires
thinkPrompt.correctAnswer: Connect handler to button click and conditionally render content

steps.anchor: We need to attach the handler to the button and make content appear only when state is true.
steps.expectedOutcome: Button triggers toggle on click, content appears only when visible.
successCriteria: Handler is attached to button onClick
Content div renders conditionally based on state
Button text or behavior reflects the toggle
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created a fully functional, type-safe toggle component!
steps.feedbackPartial: Close! Make sure both the click handler and conditional rendering are implemented.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's complete the wiring. Connect handler to button and conditionally show content.
